short: Two centuries in which Russia became a European great power and then collapsed.
full:
The Senate proclaimed Peter I emperor in 1721 after victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War, converting the Tsardom of Muscovy into an empire on the European model, with a new capital at St Petersburg, a Table of Ranks that tied noble status to state service, and a conscript army. Catherine II took the Crimea and the largest share of partitioned Poland; Alexander I's troops entered Paris in 1814. By 1900 the empire reached from Warsaw to the Pacific and covered about a sixth of the world's land surface.

It never closed the gap between that reach and its internal arrangements. Serfdom was abolished in 1861 without giving peasants enough land or releasing them from redemption payments; defeat by Japan in 1905 forced a constitution and a weak Duma. The First World War broke the railways and the bread supply to Petrograd, and after a week of strikes Nicholas II abdicated on 15 March 1917. He and his family were shot at Yekaterinburg the following year.
